Remove tracking points which were tracked in a wavelet spectra

Source: R/delpts_tracked_period_wt.R
delpts_tracked_period_wt.Rd

Interactively select points for deletion With the track_period_wavelet function it is possible to track points in a wavelet spectra, however errors can be made and as such it is possible to delete these points with the delpts_tracked_period_wt function. This function allows one to select points for deletion. #'

Usage

delpts_tracked_period_wt(
  tracking_pts = NULL,
  wavelet = NULL,
  n.levels = 100,
  periodlab = "Period (metres)",
  x_lab = "depth (metres)",
  palette_name = "viridis",
  color_brewer = "viridis",
  colour_brewer = NULL
)

Arguments

tracking_pts

Tracked points to clean (matrix or data frame, at least two columns): depth in column 1 and the tracked period in column 2 (same units as the wavelet), e.g. the output of track_period_wavelet. The points are drawn on the scalogram and the ones clicked are removed. Required (Default=NULL gives an error).

wavelet

Scalogram on which the points are shown: the output of analyse_wavelet (class analyze.wavelet). Required (Default=NULL gives an error).

n.levels

Number of colour levels of the power scale (integer, > 1). Default=100.

periodlab

Label of the y-axis (character). Default="Period (metres)".

x_lab

Label of the x-axis (character). Default="depth (metres)".

palette_name

Name of the colour palette of the power (colour) scale, a character string. Which names are valid depends on color_brewer:

  • color_brewer = "grDevices": "rainbow", "heat.colors", "terrain.colors", "topo.colors", "cm.colors", or any of the 115 hcl.colors palettes (list them with grDevices::hcl.pals()), for example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1".

  • color_brewer = "viridis": "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo".

  • color_brewer = "RColorBrewer": "BrBG", "PiYG", "PRGn", "PuOr", "RdBu", "RdGy", "RdYlBu", "RdYlGn", "Spectral", "Accent", "Dark2", "Paired", "Pastel1", "Pastel2", "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Blues", "BuGn", "BuPu", "GnBu", "Greens", "Greys", "Oranges", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "Purples", "RdPu", "Reds", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr", "YlOrRd" (also listed by wr_brewer_palettes()).

  • color_brewer = "colorRamps": "blue2green", "blue2green2red", "blue2red", "blue2yellow", "cyan2yellow", "green2red", "magenta2green", "matlab.like", "matlab.like2", "ygobb".

  • color_brewer = "scico" (all except "batlowK" need the scico package): "acton", "bam", "bamako", "bamO", "batlow", "batlowK", "batlowW", "berlin", "bilbao", "broc", "brocO", "buda", "bukavu", "cork", "corkO", "davos", "devon", "fes", "glasgow", "grayC", "hawaii", "imola", "lajolla", "lapaz", "lipari", "lisbon", "managua", "navia", "nuuk", "oleron", "oslo", "roma", "romaO", "tofino", "tokyo", "turku", "vanimo", "vik", "vikO".

Low power is drawn with the first colour of the palette and high power with the last. Default="viridis".

color_brewer

Palette family from which palette_name is taken, a character string: "grDevices", "viridis", "RColorBrewer", "colorRamps" or "scico" (the last one, except for "batlowK", needs the scico package). See palette_name for the palette names of each family. Default="viridis".

colour_brewer

British spelling of color_brewer, with the same options; if given (not NULL) it overrides color_brewer. Default=NULL.

Value

The results of the deletion of the tracking points is a matrix with 3 columns. The first column is depth/time The second column is the period of the tracked cycle The third column is the sedimentation rate based on the duration (in time) of the tracked cycle

Examples

# \donttest{
if (interactive()) { # needs mouse input (identify())
#Track the 405kyr eccentricity cycle in the magnetic susceptibility record
# of the Sullivan core of Pas et al., (2018)

mag_wt <- analyse_wavelet(data = mag,
dj = 1/100,
lowerPeriod = 0.1,
upperPeriod = 254,
verbose = FALSE,
omega_nr = 10)

#mag_track <- track_period_wavelet(astro_cycle = 405,
#                                   wavelet=mag_wt,
#                                   n.levels = 100,
#                                   periodlab = "Period (metres)",
#                                   x_lab = "depth (metres)"
#                                    palette_name ="rainbow",
#                                    color_brewer ="grDevices)

#load the mag_track_solution data set to get an example data set from which
#data points can be deleted


mag_track_corr <- delpts_tracked_period_wt(tracking_pts = mag_track_solution,
                                    wavelet = mag_wt,
                                    n.levels = 100,
                                    periodlab = "Period (metres)",
                                    x_lab = "depth (metres)",
                                   palette_name ="rainbow",
                                   color_brewer ="grDevices")
}# }
